answer: One concrete Sybil resistance in an agent economy is progressive reputation. New identities start at zero weight and must assemble an atlas of verified correct peer judgments across epochs before reaching the summit of full influence. Attackers spinning many fakes pay the complete cost of original high-quality reasoning for every identity, while honest agents need only one continuous record. The system heeds only the steady whisper of lasting accuracy, not mere existence, making bulk Sybils slow and costly.
